title: Facility Maintenance and Repair Services, APS Zutendaal, Belgium
description: The Regional Contracting Office (RCO) Benelux is issuing this Sources Sought as a means of conducting market research to identify local vendors capable of serving as the prime contractor who have an interest in the requirement for Facility Maintenance & Repair Services at APS Zutendaal in Belgium. The intention is to procure these services on a competitive basis. The contract type is anticipated to be Firm Fixed Price Indefinite Delivery/Indefinity Quantity (IDIQ) and the estimated period of performance is expected to be seven years (seven ordering periods). The performance is estimated to commence in May of 2027. Telephone inquiries will not be accepted or acknowledged, and no feedback or evaluations will be provided to companies regarding their submissions. Place of performance: APS Zutendaal, Leutsestraat 34, 3690 Zutendaal, Belgium. REQUIRED CAPABILITIES The Contractor shall perform Preventive Maintenance, Inspections, Labeling, Testing, On-call Maintenance, Repairs (to include replacement parts) of facilities, equipment, and systems which shall consist of, but not limited to: Air Conditioning systems, Exhaust Extraction system, Heating systems, Heating Pumps, Electric Heaters, Safety Emergency Lighting, including, fluorescent and streetlights, Water Lifting Stations, Boilers, Distribution lines, Heat controls, Heat Oil Storage and Delivery System, Radiators, Underground Pipes, Water and Sewer Lines, Storm Water system, Roof Drains, Roof Vents, Chimney Tower Emissions/Structure, Dehumidification Systems, Lights, Generators, Lightning Protection Systems, High/Medium Voltage Transformers and Switching Stations, POL Pumps, Leakage Protection systems and Underground Fuel Tanks, Ceiling Fan Coil Units, Manholes /Manhole Frame, ventilations, etc. If your organization has the potential capacity to perform these contract services, please provide the following information: 1) Organization name, address, email address, Web site address, telephone number, and size and type of ownership for the organization; and 2) Answers on next questions/statements: Are you interested in participating in the "Request for Quotations" (RFQ) solicitation? Are you able to provide a Firm Fixed Price for a period of performance of 7 years? (Firm fixed pricing means established firm pricing per ordering period which can reflect increases between each period. No pricing is requested at this time). Is your company familiar with working with the US Government? ADDITIONAL INFORMATION AND SUBMISSION DETAILS All responses or questions you might have under this Sources Sought must be e-mailed to both: the Contract Specialist, Sandra Van Beneden, at sandra.r.vanbeneden.ln@army.mil and the Contracting Officer, Victoria Schermerhorn, at victoria.e.schermerhorn.civ@army.mil. title: Digital Talent Services
description: Public Safety's Digital Services Directorate (DSD) is responsible for delivering and supporting the department's service, digital, data and technology capabilities. DSD works as a strategic partner to help programs deliver reliable, accessible and user-centered digital services and achieve intended outcomes. DSD must modernize aging applications, expand platform-based solutions and automation, improve service delivery and support defined project and technology-service transitions. This requirement is structured around four finite departmental initiatives, forecast work volumes and outcome-based deliverables. Contractor services will be authorized only through Task Authorizations that identify a named project, release or service package; finite scope; deliverables; milestones; level of effort; acceptance criteria; and the TBIPS category and level required to complete the work. PS requires task-based IT professional services to produce defined outcomes under the following four initiatives. Each category has one primary initiative and is not duplicated across initiatives.

title: Benchtop Multiple Reactor Systems
description: Solicitation Number: 26-58202 Publication Date: October 27, 2026 Closing Date and Time: November 24, 2026, at 2:00 PM EST Trade Agreements: • Canadian Free Trade Agreement (CFTA) (formerly Agreement on Internal Trade [AIT]) • Canada-Chile Free Trade Agreement (CCFTA) • Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP) • Canada-Colombia Free Trade Agreement (CCoFTA) • Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) • Canada–Honduras Free Trade Agreement • Canada–Korea Free Trade Agreement • Canada–Panama Free Trade Agreement • Canada–Peru Free Trade Agreement • Canada–Ukraine Free Trade Agreement • Canada-United Kingdom Trade Continuity Agreement • World Trade Organization – Agreement on Government Procurement (WTO-AGP) Region of Opportunity: • Canada (or certain provinces/territories) Region of Delivery: • Canada (or certain provinces/territories) GSIN: 41110000 Notice Type: • Request for Proposal (RFP) Tendering Procedure: • Open Description: The Clean Energy Innovation (CEI) Research Center of the National Research Council of Canada (NRC) has a requirement for the supply of two benchtop multiple reactor systems. The first system requires integrated sampling automation that can be coupled to a self-driving acceleration platform. The system will be utilized for high-throughput characterization of hydrometallurgical processes that contain multi-component mixtures in real-time as a part of the Critical Battery Materials Initiative (CBMI). The systems must be equipped to collect aliquots of reaction accurately during hydrometallurgical testing. The second system will be utilized for high-throughput characterization of crystallization processes from multi-component mixtures in real-time. This particular system must be equipped with multiple reactors to monitor turbidity, solubility, nucleation time and crystallization reactions accurately during hydrometallurgical testing. Beyond the already planned projects involving this equipment, the applications of this equipment are broad and can be incorporated into many NRC-Mississauga (NRC-M) projects. The units are expected to be received within 8 weeks of contract award. Solicitation of Offer Submission Eligibility. This solicitation of offers is subject to the Policy on Reciprocal Procurement. This means that only Canadian Suppliers and Suppliers of an Applicable Trading Partner, are eligible for this solicitation of offers. Offers submitted by Suppliers of a Non-Trading Partner will be rejected. Basis of selection: Lowest evaluated price A bid must comply with the requirements of the bid solicitation and meet all mandatory technical evaluation criteria to be declared responsive. The responsive bid with the lowest evaluated price will be recommended for award of a contract. Tenders must be submitted to the NRC Bid Receiving Unit at: NRC.BidReceiving-ReceptiondesSoumissions.CNRC@nrc-cnrc.gc.ca Refer to the attached tender documents to obtain further information. title: Puitejärjestely, murskeiden hankinta 2027-2028
description: Puitejärjestely, murskeiden hankinta 2027-2028 Metsähallitus Metsätalous Oy ja Metsähallitus Luontopalvelut (myöhemmin Metsähallitus) hankkii metsätielle, rakennushankkeisiin sekä purokunnostuksiin murskeita ja kutusoraa joko maa-ainesvarastolta (montulta) tai metsätielle toimitettuna ja levitettynä (sorastuksen palvelukuvaus liite 1). Tarjoaja voi tarjota tarjouksessaan myös myymänsä maa-aineksen kuljetusta, jolloin hän tarjoaa kertoimen suhteessa sorastuksen taksataulukkoon (liite 2). Tarjoaja voi tarjouksessaan kieltäytyä myymästä maa-aineksia muutoin kuin tielle toimitettuna. Tarjouksessa tulee ilmoittaa maa-ainespaikan sijainti ja tarjottavat murskeet hintoineen varastolla. Tarjousten perusteella Metsähallitus hyväksyy toimittajat puitejärjestelyyn. Puitejärjestely alkaa 1.1.2027 ja päättyy 31.12.2028. Tarjottuihin hintoihin sovelletaan liitteen 5 mukaista indeksiehtoa. Sekä tarjottu murskeen hinta että kuljetuksen maksukerroin nousee tai laskee indeksiehdon mukaisesti. Kuhunkin käyttökohteeseen Metsähallitus vertailee puitejärjestelyyn hyväksyttyjen tarjoajien maa-ainespaikkojen sijaintia, tarjontaa ja hintoja. Murske hankitaan kokonaiskustannukseltaan edullisimmalta tarjoajalta. Murskeen monttuhintaan lisätään tällöin kuljetuskustannus murskeen myyjän tai Metsähallituksen sopimuskumppanin kalustolla. Ennen tilausta tai sopimusta tilaaja selvittää saatavuuden tarjoajan yhteyshenkilöltä. Metsähallitus pidättää oikeuden käyttää omia murskeitaan riippumatta puitejärjestelyyn hyväksytyistä tarjouksista. Metsähallitus pidättää myös oikeuden hankkia murskeita muilta toimittajilta, mikäli puitejärjestelyyn hyväksytyiltä maa-ainespaikoilta ei löydy tarvittavaa mursketta kohtuulliselta etäisyydeltä (alle 20 km). Metsähallituksen hallinnoimien alueiden sijainti on esitetty www.retkikartta.fi. Valitse Karttatasot - Metsätalouden monikäyttömetsät - Suojelu- ja retkeilyalueet sekä sopiva taustakartta. Mikäli yksittäisen hankinnan arvo ylittää kansallisen kynnysarvon (60 000 €), siitä laaditaan sopimus (liite 3a). Mikäli yksittäisen hankinnan arvo ylittää EU-kynnysarvon (1.1.2026 alkaen 216 000 €), toimittajan tulee toimittaa rikosrekisteriotteet. Kynnysarvoja pienemmistä hankinnoista Metsähallitus laatii tilauksen (ks. liitteet 3c ja 3d).,

title: Kodinkoneet 2027-2029 Mikalo Oy, Mikkelin asumisoikeus Oy
description: Kodinkoneet 2027-2029 Mikalo Oy, Mikkelin asumisoikeus Oy Mikalo Oy ja Mikkelin Asumisoikeus Oy kilpailuttavat yhdessä kodinkonehankinnat. Hankinnan kohteena on kylmäkoneita, lattialiesiä sekä mikroaaltouuneja. Sopimuskausi on 3 vuotta, ja tilaaja varaa oikeuden hyödyntää kahden (2) vuoden optiokauden. Kaikki laitteet hankitaan kokonaispalveluna asennettuina, ja tarjotun laitehinnan on aina sisällettävä kuljetus, kerroksiinkanto, asennus käyttövalmiiksi, sähkö- tai liitäntätyöt sekä vanhan laitteen poiskuljetus ja kierrätys. Hankinnan laajuus, rajaukset ja sopimuskauden aikaiset muutokset: 1. Mikkelin kaupungin kohteiden rajaus (Ehdollinen optio): Kilpailutuksen tuloksena syntyvää puitejärjestelyä voivat hyödyntää Mikalo Oy:n ja Mikkelin Asumisoikeus Oy:n lisäksi myös Mikkelin kaupunki. Kaupungin osalta sopimus rajataan koskemaan ainoastaan niitä Mikkelin kaupungin omistuksessa olevia vuokra-asuntoja, joita Mikalo Oy isännöi tai ylläpitää. Sopimus ei koske kaupungin muita toimitiloja, virastoja tai laitoksia. Hankintayksikkö pidättää oikeuden laajentaa tilauksia koskemaan näitä kaupungin vuokra-asuntoja, mikäli/jos kyseisiä asuntokantoja siirtyy sopimuskauden aikana suoraan Mikalon hallintaan tai omistukseen. Mikkelin kaupungin osalta tarve koskee satunnaisia ja vähäisiä kodinkonehankintoja sopimuskauden aikana. 2. Uudisrakentaminen, peruskorjaukset ja suurten erien toimitusehdot: Tätä puitesopimusta voidaan hyödyntää vuokrataloyhtiöiden juoksevien arjen korvaushankintojen lisäksi myös hankintayksiköiden omissa uudisrakennus- ja peruskorjauskohteissa (esim. linjasaneeraukset ja perusparannukset). Suurissa peruskorjaus- ja uudiskohteissa, joissa laitteita tilataan kerralla yhteen osoitteeseen yli kymmenen (10) kappaletta, toimitusaika ja logistiikka sovitaan erikseen tapauskohtaisesti hankintayksikön ja toimittajan kesken rakennustyömaan aikataulun mukaan. title: Timber Bastion Rehabilitation - Fort Langley National Historic Site
description: BIDS RECEIVED BY FAX AND EMAIL WILL BE ACCEPTED AS OFFICIAL. PARKS CANADA IS NOT CURRENTLY ACCEPTING BIDS VIA SAP ARIBA, YOU MUST SUBMIT YOUR BID VIA FAX OR EMAIL AS INDICATED IN THE SOLICITATION DOCUMENT. BIDS RECEIVED IN-PERSON OR BY COURIER WILL NOT BE ACCEPTED. The only acceptable email address for responses to bid solicitations is soumissionsami-bidsrpc@pc.gc.ca. Bids submitted by email directly to the Contracting Authority or to any email address other than soumissionsami-bidsrpc@pc.gc.ca will not be accepted. The only acceptable facsimile for responses to bid solicitations is 1-855-983-1808. The maximum email file size that Parks Canada is capable of receiving is 15 megabytes. The Bidder is responsible for any failure attributable to the transmission or receipt of the emailed bid due to file size. The Bidder should be cognisant of the size of the email as a whole, and not only the attachments. Please take into consideration that some attachments, when sent, may be resized during the email transfer. If the email size is too large, the Bidder should send the bid in multiple emails properly labeled with the solicitation number, project name, and indicate how many emails are included (ex. 1 of 2). Emails with links to bid documents will not be accepted. Bid documents must be sent as email attachments. REQUIREMENT The Parks Canada Agency (PCA) has a requirement for qualified Contractor to dismantle the northwest (NW) bastion structure at Fort Langley National Historic Site (FLNHS) and purchase new timbers for future reconstruction. The contractor is only responsible for the scope described in the Statement of Work; the reassembly of the bastion is not a part of this project scope. TWO-SUBMISSION BID This Bid shall be submitted following a “two-submission” procedure. Refer to SI04 of the Special Instructions to Bidders. CONTRACTOR SELECTION AND INDIGENOUS PARTICIPATION PLAN The Contractor should ensure provision of specific and agreed upon benefits for Indigenous People and Indigenous Businesses in the Area of the Contract. This Invitation to Tender contains bid criteria in order to provide socioeconomic benefits to Indigenous communities within the area covered by the contract. PERIOD OF CONTRACT / DELIVERY DATE Contractor shall perform and complete the Work no later than March 31, 2027. OPTIONAL SITE VISIT It is recommended that the Bidder or a representative of the Bidder visit the work site. Arrangements have been made for the site visit to be held at the entrance to Fort Langley National Historic Site at 23433 Mavis Ave, Langley Twp, BC V1M 3R6 on November 18, 2026. The site visit will begin 10:00 AM (Pacific Time). Bidders should communicate with the Contracting Authority no later than November 17, 2026, at 10:00 AM (Pacific Time).to confirm attendance and provide the name(s) of the person(s) who will attend. Bidders must also complete and submit a certification. Bidders who do not confirm attendance, provide the name(s) of the person(s) who will attend, or who do not complete and submit the above certification as required will not be allowed access to the site. Bidders will be requested to sign an attendance sheet. No alternative appointment will be given to bidders who do not attend or do not send a representative. Bidders who do not participate in the visit will not be precluded from submitting a bid. Any clarifications or changes to the bid solicitation resulting from the site visit will be included as an amendment to the bid solicitation. ENQUIRIES All enquiries of a technical and contractual nature are to be submitted to the Contracting Authority. Enquiries regarding this solicitation must be submitted in writing and should be received no later than five (5) business days prior to the date set for solicitation closing to allow sufficient time to provide a response. Enquiries received after that time may result in an answer NOT being provided. INFORMATION National Parks Regulations require that all work is to be performed in accordance with the ordinances, laws, rules and regulations set out in the National Park Act. Bidders that consider themselves qualified to provide this Work and intend to submit bids on this project should obtain documents from the Government Electronic Tendering Service through the Government of Canada tendering service at http://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities. Addenda, when issued, will be available from the Government of Canada tendering service. Bidders that elect to base their bids on documents obtained from other sources do so at their own risk. Late submissions will not be considered. The Crown retains the right to negotiate with suppliers on any procurement. Documents may be submitted in either official language of Canada. Parks Canada has made every effort to provide equivalent documents in both official languages, however, if you find any discrepancies between the English and French documents, please notify the contract officer listed in this opportunity as soon as possible so that we can rectify the situation.

title: Belgium – Laboratory, optical and precision equipments (excl. glasses) – Purchase, delivery, installation and commissioning of a multi-wavelength orthogonal tomographic volumetric 3D printing system
description: This contract concerns the purchase, delivery, installation, commissioning and handover of a fully operational multi-wavelength orthogonal tomographic volumetric 3D printing system for scientific research. Explanation: The infrastructure is intended for advanced research in tomographic volumetric 3D printing, in which multiple optical wavelengths can be controlled independently to achieve spatial control over different photochemical processes. The system must enable research into multi-wavelength and multi-material tomographic 3D printing. The contract comprises a complete and fully integrated system, including all optical, mechanical and electronic components, light sources, control hardware and software, safety equipment and accessories required for its intended operation. The contract includes delivery of the complete system and all required accessories; installation and commissioning at Ghent University; system configuration, calibration and functional verification; provision of the necessary control and processing software; user training; user and technical documentation; and technical support, warranty and maintenance as further specified in the tender specifications.

title: Netherlands – Sanitary paper products – SARO Europese aanbesteding sanitaire voorzieningen 2026
description: Deze Offerteaanvraag betreft de Europese openbare Aanbesteding Sanitaire voorzieningen waarop de meest recente versie van de Aanbestedingswet 2012 (Aw-2012) van toepassing is. De aanbesteding heeft betrekking op het leveren, beheren, onderhouden en vervangen van sanitaire voorzieningen ten behoeve van Stichting Samen Ambitieus Rotterdams Onderwijs (SARO), hierna tenoemen de Aanbestedende dienst of Opdrachtgever. De geraamde waarde van deze opdracht bedraagt circa € 3 miljoen exclusief btw, inclusief de maximale looptijd van de overeenkomst en alle verlengingsopties. Deze raming is gebaseerd op historische uitgaven van SARO, de huidige omvang van de organisatie, de verwachte gefaseerde instroom van locaties en de uitgangspunten van deze aanbesteding. De raming is indicatief en kan tot ±30% afwijken als gevolg van wijzigingen in locaties, leerling- en medewerkers aantallen, gebruiksintensiteit of andere relevante omstandigheden. Aan deze raming kunnen geen rechten worden ontleend.

title: Angler Mine Neutralization Remotely Operated Vehicle (ROV) Systems and Support
description: Description This presolicitation notice is published to announce that Direct Reporting Program Manager for Robotic and Autonomous Systems (DRPM RAS) intends to award a Firm Fixed Price sole-source contract to Advanced Acoustic Concepts, LLC (AAC), 425 Oser Avenue, Hauppauge, NY 11788 (CAGE: 4GPS8) for the procurement of Angler Mine Neutralization Remotely Operated Vehicle (ROV) Systems, operator consoles, reload kits, depot-level testing, spares, peculiar support equipment, and associated technical, logistics, and software engineering services. This requirement will be negotiated on a sole-source basis in accordance with statutory authority 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), as implemented by FAR 6.103-1 (RFO) (Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements). The system was matured across prior competitive Office of Naval Research (ONR) Science & Technology (S&T) contracts N00014-18-C-1027 and N00014-21-C-1006, and initial low-rate operational fielding under N66604-24-D-C401. AAC is the original designer, developer, systems integrator, and sole manufacturer of the Angler platform. The Government does not possess a complete, validated Technical Data Package (TDP) suitable for competition production, integration, qualification, and safety certification of the existing Angler configuration. Specifically, the Government has only Limited and Restricted Rights to the core system architecture, including the deep-water 20mm standoff projectile design, gun subsystem, and the proprietary Navigation and Control (NAC) software suite. Award to any other source would result in a substantial duplication of cost to the Government not expected to be recovered through competition and would cause unacceptable developmental and safety-certification delays. This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals. However, all responsible sources may submit a capability statement, which shall be considered by the agency. Interested sources shall identify their capability to satisfy the requirement; relevant technical, production, integration, and support experience; and any material assumptions, Government-furnished information, technical-data rights, software rights, interfaces, qualification activities, or transition period necessary to perform. Responses shall be submitted by 1000 on 24 November 2026 to the contacts listed in this posting.

title: Weapons Effects Solicitation
description: This solicitation is related to Notice IDs: N00167-25-RFP-CD-66-001 and N00167-25-RFP-CD-66-001_Rev1. The contractor shall provide scientific and technical services with experts in UNDEX and AIREX analysis of undersea and surface vessels to develop and utilize specialized software codes that: 1) Aid in the selection of live fire events and provide support to live fire test and evaluation programs; 2) Simulate an underwater shock environment from a far field or near miss location; 3) Simulate the response of Navy platforms to UNDEX and AIREX for far field, near miss, contact, and internally detonating weapon attacks; 4) Check the integrity of computational models; 5) Solve finite element models elastic-plastic response and reduced order engineering tools to UNDEX and AIREX events; and 6) Simulate a nuclear underwater shock environment or nuclear air blast environment from a far field location. This opportunity is for SEAPORT-NxG MAC HOLDERS ONLY- UNRESTRICTED. No other offers will be considered. Proposals submitted by non-MAC holders will not be evaluated. Please note the Navy has transitioned from the legacy SeaPort portal to the PIEE Solicitation Module for the submission of offers, proposals, and awards under SeaPort-NxG. SeaPort MAC holders will need to register for PIEE accounts in order to receive solicitations and submit proposals/offers. Please reference the official Department of Defense registration guide for vendors on how to set up accounts in PIEE:https://www.acq.osd.mil/asda/dpc/ce/cap/docs/piee/PIEE_Solicitation_Module_Vendor_Access_Instructions.pdf. Provision L-215-H006 (c) states that all questions shall be submitted via email to the Primary and Secondary Solicitation Managers identified in the Solicitation Module HOWEVER all questions shall be submitted via the PIEE Solicitation Module Question and Answer Function. Responses will be posted within the PIEE Solicitation Module. The solicitation will be amended to reflect the correct submission procedures for questions. *Manual upload to Contract Opportunities in SAM.gov as all previous attempts to post failed*

title: Weapons Effect Solicitation
description: This solicitation is related to Notice IDs: N00167-25-RFP-CD-66-0014 and N00167-25-RFP-CD-66-0014_Rev1. The contractor shall provide scientific and technical services with experts in UNDEX and AIREX analysis of undersea and surface vessels to develop and utilize specialized software codes that: 1) Aid in the selection of live fire events and provide support to live fire test and evaluation programs; 2) Simulate an underwater shock environment from a far field or near miss location; 3) Simulate the response of Navy platforms to UNDEX and AIREX for far field, near miss, contact, and internally detonating weapon attacks; 4) Check the integrity of computational models; 5) Solve finite element models elastic-plastic response and reduced order engineering tools to UNDEX and AIREX events; and 6) Simulate a nuclear underwater shock environment or nuclear air blast environment from a far field location. This opportunity is for SEAPORT-NxG MAC HOLDERS ONLY- UNRESTRICTED. No other offers will be considered. Proposals submitted by non-MAC holders will not be evaluated. title: Switzerland – Architectural, construction, engineering and inspection services – Sanierung Bodensee-Arena Leistungsofferte HLKS inkl. Gebäudeautomation und Fachkoordination
description: La Bodensee-Arena est un complexe sportif, de loisirs et d'événements majeur de la région de Kreuzlingen-Constance. Créé en 1978 et agrandi à plusieurs reprises, ce complexe présente un besoin important de rénovation sur les plans architectural, technique et opérationnel. La ville de Kreuzlingen prévoit la rénovation du complexe existant et la transformation de l'actuelle patinoire extérieure en salle d'entraînement. La structure existante doit être réutilisée dans la mesure où cela s’avère techniquement et économiquement justifié. La réalisation se fera par étapes, en tenant compte de l’exploitation en cours. Le crédit d’investissement de 26,7 millions de francs suisses a été approuvé lors du référendum du 28 septembre 2025. Ce montant constitue le plafond financier contraignant de l’ensemble du projet. La conception doit être développée de manière cohérente selon le principe du « Design-to-Cost ». Dans le cadre d’une procédure d’appel d’offres sélective avec préqualification (phase 1) suivie d’une soumission d’offres (phase 2), un bureau d’études qualifié en CVC est recherché pour la conception CVC, y compris l’automatisation du bâtiment (MSRL) et la coordination technique. Le bureau doit couvrir l’ensemble des domaines techniques faisant l’objet de l’appel d’offres et assumer la responsabilité globale de la coordination et de l’intégration des prestations dans le cadre du mandat. Le mandat comprend les prestations prévues par la norme SIA 108 pour les phases 31 à 53, de la conception à la mise en service. Les différents niveaux de modernisation des installations techniques existantes, l'intégration de la récupération de la chaleur résiduelle provenant du système de refroidissement de la patinoire, ainsi que la coordination de l'approvisionnement en énergie et des installations techniques dans le bâtiment principal existant et dans la nouvelle salle d'entraînement constituent des défis particuliers. Il s’agit de trouver des solutions économiques et efficaces sur le plan énergétique, qui tiennent compte des différentes utilisations et conditions d’exploitation et permettent une réalisation par étapes tout en préservant autant que possible le fonctionnement courant. Les interfaces avec les études de réfrigération et d’électricité, faisant l’objet de marchés distincts, doivent être assurées.

title: Switzerland – Architectural, construction, engineering and inspection services – Sanierung Bodensee-Arena Leistungsofferte Elektroplanung
description: La Bodensee-Arena est un complexe sportif, de loisirs et d'événements majeur de la région de Kreuzlingen-Constance. Créé en 1978 et agrandi à plusieurs reprises, ce complexe présente un besoin important de rénovation sur les plans architectural, technique et opérationnel. La ville de Kreuzlingen prévoit la rénovation du complexe existant et la transformation de l'actuelle patinoire extérieure en salle d'entraînement. Dans le cadre d’une procédure d’appel d’offres sélective avec préqualification (phase 1) suivie d’une soumission d’offres (phase 2), un bureau d’études en électrotechnique qualifié est recherché pour la conception électrique, y compris les installations photovoltaïques. Le mandat comprend les prestations prévues par la norme SIA 108 pour les phases 31 à 53, de la conception à la mise en service, y compris la conception des installations à courant fort et à courant faible ainsi que des installations photovoltaïques. Les différents niveaux de modernisation des installations électriques existantes, le renouvellement des câbles et des tableaux de distribution, ainsi que l’intégration des installations photovoltaïques dans l’infrastructure électrique constituent des défis particuliers. Les interfaces avec les systèmes CVC et d’automatisation du bâtiment, pour lesquels des marchés distincts ont été passés, avec la conception du système de refroidissement de la patinoire ainsi qu’avec la protection contre l’incendie doivent être coordonnées et validées dès le début du projet. Nous recherchons des solutions économiques, efficaces sur le plan énergétique et fiables, qui répondent aux exigences de l’ensemble du projet et respectent le plafond budgétaire imposé.

title: Supply of SAPU Target Systems
description: Unite Procurement UK Limited (part of Unite Holding SE), on behalf of the Ministry of Defence, is seeking suppliers to join the Unite Procurement Platform to support the provision of SAPU Target Systems. Overview SAPU Target Systems represents a strategic capability requirement aimed at delivering robust, scalable, and secure target management solutions. This opportunity seeks qualified organisations with demonstrated expertise in: • Improved reliability compared to legacy SAPU systems. • Advanced remote-control functionality. • Enhanced programmability and scenario management. • Greater operational flexibility. • Reduced maintenance burden. • A proven and sustainable long-term replacement for existing target systems. The Unite Procurement Platform (Unite | Simplify indirect procurement with our smarter platform) offers a compliant route to market for UK Public Sector organisations to manage low-value, high-volume procurement. How to Apply Interested suppliers should register their interest by contacting Unite Procurement UK Limited and provide details of their product range, modification capabilities, and maintenance services. Further information on the onboarding process for the Unite Procurement Platform will be provided upon expression of interest and can also be found at the link attached. Unite Procurement UK Limited does not intend to appoint a sole supplier for this requirement. Instead, multiple suppliers may be onboarded to the Unite Procurement Platform to ensure a diverse and competitive supply base, supporting flexibility and choice for the Ministry of Defence and associated organisations. Suppliers are encouraged to express their interest by the stated closing date to ensure early consideration. However, applications to join the Unite Procurement Platform will be welcome at any time beyond the initial deadline. Unite Procurement UK Limited reserves the right to review and onboard new suppliers on a rolling basis to meet evolving requirements and to maintain a dynamic and responsive supplier network. For any enquiries and interest, please email defence.support@unite.eu with the subject title "TSS 864 Opportunity"

title: V301--539 - Fifth Floor Pharmacy Move Service Contract
description: The Cincinnati Veterans Administration Medical Center (VAMC) has a requirement to move the inpatient pharmacy to either to the second floor or the eight floor (back up eighth floor depending on room availability). The intention of this Sources Sought is to obtain information only. Please do not send a proposal. Requested information: To aid acquisition planning, we re seeking capable and interested firms for the information requested. If your firm meets the criteria please send the point of contract (ronald.heidemann@va.gov) the following, via email: Firm s Name Socio-Economic Status Whether or not your company has a contract vehicle we can order against If your company believes there is an alternative NAICS code please provide this If your company has any questions please provide. PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT 1.0 BACKGROUND The Cincinnati VA Medical Center (VAMC) will be activating a new air handler unit for pharmacy with the potential move date being late-2026/early-2027, November-May. Due to personnel constraints, we are requesting the use of specialized movers to relocate medical equipment and testing needed to keep up with current inpatient care medication. The current pharmaceutical iv hoods, 3200 Vine St., Cincinnati, OH 45220 fifth floor will be required to move to second floor (back up eighth floor depending on room availability). This will allow room certification testing so the Cincinnati pharmacy department can continue to create medications for patients within the hospital and CLC. SCOPE OF WORK The purpose of this contract is to provide relocation and moving services for the VA Medical Center at 3200 Vine St., Cincinnati, OH 45220. Moving and relocation services could include disassembly and assembly of iv hoods, disconnecting and reconnecting of medical equipment, disconnecting and reconnecting electricity from the equipment. The Contractor shall provide non-personal services, laborers, contractor operated vehicles, equipment, supplies, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, to perform relocation and moving services for Cincinnati VAMC as defined in the PWS. The contractor shall not connect to or have access to the VA Network at any time. This work should also include room recertification of the medical equipment for non-hazardous pharmacy iv hoods. Testing will allow for pharmacy to continue medication for use of patients and minimize down time of the current iv space. The contractor will then return all equipment to its original location after communicating with COR, process will take 2-4 weeks after original relocation date has been chosen. 3.0 CONTRACT TYPE Firm-Fixed Price. 4.0 PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE Due to the fluid nature of construction, there is not a set date established for the move of the facility, the current period of performance would be November 2026- May 2027. The total number of days required for the work can be established by the contractor and COR during the kick-off meeting, floor plans with the square footage will be provided by the government in the PWS to assist with planning. The government will keep the contractor informed on potential move dates weekly to ensure that proper planning can be completed. Weekend and after-hour work may be required. 5.0 PLACE OF PERFORMANCE From: The Cincinnati VAMC located at 3200 Vine St., Cincinnati, Ohio 45220 fifth floor pharmacy. To: The Cincinnati VAMC located at 3200 Vine St., Cincinnati, Ohio 45220 second floor (or eighth floor depending on room availability) . Back: To original location The Cincinnati VAMC located at 3200 Vine St., Cincinnati, Ohio 45220 fifth floor pharmacy. 6.0 TRAVEL The Government does not anticipate(s) travel under this effort. All work will be within the main Cincinnati VAMC building. 7.0 TASK STATEMENT The Contractor shall provide the following services to support the Cincinnati VAMC clinic office move operations. In addition, the Contractor shall provide all the necessary supplies, materials, equipment, and personnel to fulfil the Government s requirement. At no time during the performance of the contract shall the contractor personnel manage or oversee any federal government personnel. a. Loading and unloading equipment to move items to and from Cincinnati VAMC floors as needed. b. Delivering/hauling medical equipment, and supplies. c. Disconnection and reconnection of medical equipment, if needed, in alignment with manufacturer recommendations. d. Disconnecting and reconnecting electrical power from the workstations, if needed, in alignment with manufacturer recommendations. f. Setting up and reassembling workstations, or medical equipment, as directed by the COR in alignment with manufacturer recommendations. g. Moving and arranging medical equipment or workstations in alignment with manufacturer recommendations. h. Disassembly of medical equipment or workstations to facilitate move, if needed, in alignment with manufacturer recommendations. i. Submit Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity (CPCN) from the Ohio PUCO 48 hours in advance of any scheduled move or relocation, which shall be inclusive of driver proofs of identification, commercial licensure, certifications, and any VA security documentation (Privacy training certificate) if needed for access to Government facilities. Liability insurance as part of this certification shall eclipse the anticipated value of equipment being relocated and should cover damages to the facilities. j. Shall provide ALL packing materials (i.e. moving boxes, cartons, packing material etc.) and equipment to move requested medical equipment, workstations and supplies. k. Shall pack the equipment, furniture, and supplies into appropriate containers (e.g., boxes, bubble wrap, protective materials) to ensure safe transport and prevent damage. 7.1 Pre-Planning Meeting: Upon award of the contract, the Contractor shall schedule a pre-planning meeting with the COR no more than 7 calendar days after award, and no less than 2 calendar days prior to any relocation efforts. 7.1.1 The Contractor shall coordinate all moves required under this contract with the COR, facility management, and technical points of contact within Cincinnati VAMC. Pre-planning will incorporate site surveys before the move, the Contractor and COR s agreed upon planned approach to completing the move, scheduling specific move dates, and inventorying all equipment subject to move. 7.1.2 Pre-planning Meeting will also include coordination for loading docks, security passes, reserved cargo elevators and all other pre-planning required to complete the move. The contractor shall provide the COR and Facility Management with a Microsoft Word Document or PDF outlining the agreed upon planned approach no more than 48 hours after the pre-planning meeting. 7.1.3 Inventory Lists: The Contractor shall review inventory list of items for relocation, including but not limited to office furniture, workstations, and devices, fragile items, file cabinets, medical equipment, and any supplies or office equipment within the facility. 7.2 Relocating/Moving Services: The Contractor shall safely and effectively disassemble, pack, load, unload, unpack, reassemble, and set up moved equipment/supplies in accordance with the PWS. 7.2.1 Upon approval of the planned approach and inventory listing, the Contractor shall properly disassemble, pack, and load items not limited to workstations, appliances , fragile items, IT and medical equipment using the proper tools and equipment provided by the Contractor. Proper tools include, but are not limited to, hand operated tools, dollies, boxes, straps, stevedores, and power operated tools. 7.2.2 The Contractor shall use materials such as cardboard boxes, moving crates, plastic crates, bins, carts, e-bags, bubble wrap, furniture paddings, various floor and elevator paddings, pallets, straps, tape, and materials to safely pack furniture, equipment, devices, and any other items identified by the COR within the facility. 7.2.3

title: Oakengates Carnival and Parade - Organisation and Delivery
description: Oakengates Town Council is looking to appoint a qualified and experienced event management company to organise and deliver a carnival and parade in Oakengates, Telford in the Summer of 2027 (date to be agreed). Under the direction of the Council, the successful bidder will be responsible, for the following: • Event Planning and Coordination: develop a comprehensive plan for the carnival, including timelines, logistics, and contingency plans. • Entertainment and Activities: arrange for a diverse range of entertainment options, including live performances, games, and interactive activities. • Vendor Management: coordinate with food and merchandise vendors to ensure a wide variety of offerings. • Marketing and Promotion: develop and execute a marketing strategy to promote the event and attract attendees. • Health and Safety: ensure all health and safety regulations are met, including crowd control, first aid, and emergency procedures. • Income Generation - identify potential income generating opportunities to support the cost of the event. • Post-Event Evaluation: provide a detailed report on the event's success, including attendance figures, feedback and recommendations for future events. Interested companies are required to submit the following: • Company Profile: a brief overview of the company, including relevant experience and qualifications. • Proposed Plan: a detailed proposal outlining the approach to organising and delivering the carnival and parade. • Budget: a comprehensive budget breakdown, including all anticipated costs. • Insurance: evidence of public liability • References: contact information for at least two previous clients who can attest to the company's capabilities. Late submissions will not be considered and Oakengates Town Council reserves the right to accept or reject any or all bids. All costs incurred in the preparation of the bid are the responsibility of the bidding company. Prospective contractors must not contact Councillors or staff to encourage or support their tender outside the prescribed process. Written tenders must be received by Oakengates Town Council in a sealed envelope marked 'Oakengates Town Council - Carnival Tender' and addressed to the Town Clerk, by 5pm on Tuesday 24 November 2026 and should be sent to: Oakengates Town Council The Wakes, Theatre Square Telford, TF2 6EP If you require any further information, please contact Oakengates Town Council by: Email: townclerk@oakengates-tc.gov.uk, or telephone: 01952 567500

title: Notice to Industry - LVN B95 Fire Station Addition
description: Notice to Industry The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Kansas City District is notifying industry that the following requirement is being pursued as a Progressive Design Build Other Transaction (PDB-OT) under 10 USC 2808a, Other Transaction for Construction. This notice is for informational purposes only to notify industry and seek feedback on the strategy. Project Overview Project Title: B95 Fire Station Addition Location: Ft. Leavenworth, KS Agency: USACE, Kansas City District (NWK) NAICS Code: 236220-Commerical and Industrial Building Construction The Kansas City District is seeking a Progressive Design Build partner to design and construct an addition to Building 95, a historic fire station. If you are interested in pursuing this PDB-OT, please send an email to the addresses below. We also ask that you provide responses to the following questions to better inform our decision and strategy. Send your response to: Myleesa France at myleesa.s.france@usace.army.mil David Miller at david.f.miller@usace.army.mil Michael France at michael.g.france@usace.army.mil

title: Request for Information (RFI) for a Cislunar Space System (CSS)
description: (U) The Department of the Air Force (DAF) is seeking market research information to inform the potential acquisition strategy for a Cislunar Space System (CSS). The CSS will consist of up to five (5) space vehicles (SVs), each of which will require a spacecraft bus, accommodation of a Government-provided payload, SV integration & test, a Ground Segment, including mission management and telemetry, tracking, control and communications, a solution for space launch, system (space vehicle/ground segment/communications) integration, and operations and maintenance (O&M). The Government is notionally interested in procuring up to five (5) SVs to meet DAF mission needs in late CY29. These vehicles may serve as seed vehicles that will inform the acquisition strategy for a potential future proliferated cislunar constellation. The Government is looking for information on industry's ability to provide a rapid, low-risk (minimal non-recurring engineering (NRE)) solution that can accommodate the Government's technical and programmatic objectives. (U) The Government intends to award up to five (5) Firm Fixed Price (FFP) preliminary design study contracts upon Government consideration of the market information collected with this RFI and all other sources of information relevant to the effort. Failure to respond to this RFI may result in loss of the ability to participate in a subsequent program acquisition. (U) This RFI does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), and industry should not construe the RFI as a commitment by the Government. In accordance with Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) provision 15.101, Early Exchanges with Industry, be advised that this is only an RFI and does not obligate the Government to reimburse any cost associated with preparation and/or submission of a RFI response. This RFI does not guarantee that the Government will issue an RFP or award a contract to provide these supplies or services.

description: TITLE: Sources Sought � Design-Build (D-B) Services for the Automotive (United Auto Workers - UAW) Building E9 Roof Replacement, HVAC Replacement and Seismic Upgrades at the Clearfield Job Corps Center The US Department of Labor, Office of Job Corps Acquisition Services, has a requirement for a qualified firm to provide design/build services that include, but are not limited to, the complete design and construction for the replacement of the existing roofing system including the roof eaves, overhangs and the roof drainage systems, roof HVAC curbs, pipe penetrations, flashings, roof edge pieces, etc. as needed to provide a weathertight roof system. THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE. In accordance with Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) 10.001(b), this notice is issued for the purpose of conducting market research. Market research is being conducted to determine if there are potential small businesses with the capacity and experience to perform the required work. This Notice is not to be misconstrued as an Invitation for Bid or Request for Proposal. THERE IS NO SOLICITATION AT THIS TIME. This request for capability information does not constitute a request for proposals; submission of any information in response to this market survey is purely voluntary; the Government assumes no financial responsibility for any costs incurred. The full extent of the work will be described in the solicitation, which may follow at a later date. However, a summary of the services to be performed is provided as follows: The work includes design-build (design and construction) services for the complete design and construction for the phased replacement of the existing ballasted built-up roofing system with a new EPDM roofing system including roof eaves, overhangs, roof drainage systems, roof HVAC curbs, pipe penetrations, flashings, roof edge pieces, etc. as needed to provide a weathertight roof system for the Automotive (UAW) Building E9 which totals approximately 120,000 gross square feet (GSF). Also included is the design and construction of the replacement of roof mounted HVAC units and associated ductwork, replacement of roof mounted exhaust fans, and seismic upgrades to the building structure to bring it up to current seismic codes for Utah. The roof design shall meet current allowable wind loads for Clearfield, Utah. Work shall be in accordance with the National Roofing Contractors Association (NCRA) recommendations for the type of roofing system specified. The NAICS code for this project is 236220 with a size standard of $45 Million. The magnitude of construction for this project is more than $10 million. Firms interested in this requirement are requested to submit a statement of qualifications. Your statement of qualifications shall demonstrate the capacity of your firm to perform the services described above, and should include the following information: 1. Provide two (2) project examples where the D/B Contractor has completed (substantially or final) the design and replacement of single-ply Ethylene Propylene Diene Monomer (EPDM) roofing systems within the last five (5) years. 2. Provide two (2) project examples where the D/B Contractor has completed (substantially or final) the design and replacement of roof mounted HVAC units and associated ductwork and air devices within the last five (5) years. 3. Provide two (2) project examples where the D/B Contractor has completed (substantially or final) the design and seismic upgrades in occupied buildings within the last five (5) years. Project examples shall include the location of the project, the project owner, and a brief description of the services performed. Your synopsis should also include the date of contract award, the original and final date of contract completion. Using the previous project examples indicate the original contract price and final contract value. The Government will evaluate market information to ascertain potential market capacity to 1) provide services consistent in scope and scale with those described in this notice and otherwise anticipated; and 2) secure and apply the full range of corporate financial, human capital, and technical resources required to successfully perform similar requirements. Your submission should not exceed 10 pages. Your response to this notice, is due no later than November 24, 2026, by 2:00 PM EST, and submit it via email to Bernadette Hughes, hughes.bernadette.l@dol.gov and Martrelle Pyatt Harvin at PyattHarvin.Martrelle@dol.gov Your submission must cite the following information, at a minimum: Response to RFI 1605AE-27-N-00001; Company Name, Address, and Company Point of Contact; SAM Unique Entity Identifier (UEI); Business Size Standard/Classification, and socio-economic status, if applicable; NAICS code certifications. Acknowledgment of responses will not be made, nor will respondents be notified regarding the results of the Government�s evaluation of the information received. The determination to proceed with the acquisition is within the discretion of the Government. Telephone inquiries will not be accepted and no questions in connection with this notice will be accepted. Please be reminded that a prospective Offeror interested in obtaining a contract award with the Government must be registered in the Federal Government's System for Award Management (SAM) database. Additional information regarding contractor registration can be obtained through the following website, www.SAM.gov.

title: W9123627BA004: NASA Wallops Breakwater Project in Wallops Island, Virginia
description: This is a pre-solicitation notice. This is NOT a solicitation. Do NOT submit proposals or questions in response to this notice. It is anticipated that the solicitation will be posted on Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) website at https://piee.eb.mil/ by the end of November 2026. The solicitation is anticipated to be posted for 30 calendar days. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Norfolk District (NAO) intends to issue an Invitation for Bid (IFB) acquisition for the NASA Wallops Shoreline Breakwaters Project in Accomack County, Virginia. This procurement will be conducted in accordance with FAR Part 14, Invitation for Bid (IFB). The Government intends to award a firm-fixed-price (FFP) contract. The requirement will be solicited as a 100% small business set aside. The applicable NAICS code is 237990, Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction (Dredging and Surface Cleanup Activities), with a small business standard of $45 million. In accordance with DFARS 236.204 - Disclosure of the Magnitude of Construction Projects, the magnitude of construction is between $10,000,000 and $25,000,000. DESCRIPTION OF WORK The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers � Norfolk District is seeking eligible firms capable of constructing breakwaters along the beach of Wallops Island. The number of proposed breakwaters for this project will be between two to four and placed approximately 200 feet offshore (from Mean High Water elevation). Each breakwater will be constructed of Type II rip rap for armor stone and VDOT Class III stone for core stone. The weight of material for each breakwater is approximately 10,000 tons. Breakwaters are to be placed on 12-inch-thick marine mattress with geotextile fabric. Water depths for breakwater placement range between -9.5 ft and -12.0 ft NAVD88. Each breakwater will be constructed to a crest height of +7 ft NAVD88. Material for breakwaters may be transported to the project site either by land or sea. Construction of breakwaters may occur either by land or sea. Various work restrictions are expected due to active rocket launches within the vicinity of the project site, which will require all construction activities to stop and personnel to vacate the premises for hours to day(s). The construction completion date will be approximately 325 calendar days from the issuance of Notice to Proceed (NTP). Contractors will be required to submit bid bonds documents with the proposal. The successful awardee will be required to provide 100% payment and performance bonds for the project. The effort will be solicited and awarded utilizing the Sealed Bid procedures under FAR Part 14. Anticipated solicitation issuance time frame is on or about the end of November 2026. THIS PROJECT IS A 100% SMALL BUSINESS SET ASIDE PROCUREMENT INVITATION FOR SEALED BID. The Government intends to award a firm fixed price contract using INVITATION FOR BID WITH PRE-AWARD SURVEY and procedures outlined in FAR 36 and FAR 14. Pre-award survey will determine contractor responsibility in accordance with FAR 9.104. Bidders will be evaluated on both pre-award survey and conformance to the solicitation and price. The Government reserves the right to reject any or all Bids; and to award the contract to other than the lowest total price and to award to the bidder submitting the lowest bid determined by the Government to be responsible. Bid bonds will be required with bid submittals. In addition, the awardee must be found responsible in accordance with FAR 9.1. title: AN/SPY-6(V) FY27-FY36 Hardware, Production, and Sustainment
description: Disclaimer: This pre-solicitation notice is for information only, and shall not be construed as a commitment by the Government to solicit contractual offers or award contracts. The Government will not reimburse the cost of any submission in response to this announcement � the entire cost of any submission will be at the sole expense of the source submitting the information. If a solicitation is issued in the future, it will be announced separately on SAM.gov and all interested parties must comply with that announcement. The Government will not reimburse respondents for any questions submitted or information provided as a result of this notice. Submission of a response to this notice does not constitute a request to be added to a bidders list or receive a copy of a future solicitation. Synopsis The U.S Navy must maintain and modernize to meet current and future operational requirements. The Portfolio Acquisition Executive Mission Systems (PAE MS) intends to issue the competitive solicitation N61750-27-R-1402 for an Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity-Multiple Award Contract (IDIQ-MAC) for the procurement of AN/SPY-6(V) Hardware, Production, and Sustainment efforts. The Government intends to utilize the IDIQ-MAC to support current and future AN/SPY-6(V) systems and subsystems, including products and/or services to design, develop, fabricate, prototype, integrate, test, maintain, and support the multiple variants of the AN/SPY-6(V). The anticipated period of performance of the base period shall be approximately five (5) years from the date of contract award with the potential of a five (5) year ordering period option. The AN/SPY-6(V) Family of Radar (FoR) systems are designed to be scalable and adaptable across multiple ship classes and mission requirements. The AN/SPY-6(V)1, which is the Navy�s next generation radar system that will address Ballistic Missile Defense (BMD) and Air Defense (AD) capability gaps identified in the Maritime Air and Missile Defense of Joint Forces (MAMDJF) Initial Capabilities Document (ICD), will provide the capabilities defined by the AMDR Capabilities Production Document (CPD). AN/SPY-6(V)2, a rotating phased array, will be the primary radar for self-defense and situational awareness and the backup radar for ATC on NIMITZ class CVNs and large deck amphibious platforms. AN/SPY-6(V)3, a 3-face fixed phased array. EASR will be the primary air surveillance radar supporting ship self-defense, situational awareness and Air Traffic Control (ATC) for Ford Class Carriers (CVN 79+) and air defense for the Constellation Class Frigates. The AN/SPY-6(V)4 system is a variant of AMDR sized for retrofit into DDG Flight IIA ships to support modernization upgrades in Integrated Air and Missile Defense capability. Sources sought notices N00024-25-R-5510, N00024-25-R-551X, and N00024-25-R-55XX were issued related to this synopsis on SAM.gov and were most recently updated on 1 September 2026. It should be noted that merely expressing interest (to include any response generated by artificial intelligence) and/or failing to demonstrate your company�s ability to meet the requirements identified above will not be considered.

title: RFI Contractor F-16 Pilot Services
description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION Title: �RFI Contractor F-16 Pilot Services� Notice ID: FA823226ACFERRY USAF/AFMC/AFLCMC/F-16-SPO/FMS Contracting Office, Hill Air Force Base, UT Description 1.1 The F-16 Support Program Office in support of the FMS countries is seeking information on how an interested contractor could provide Contractor F-16 Pilot Services � Ferry Flight Operations for Two (2) F-16 Block 52 Fighting Falcon Aircraft (Lockheed Martin Facility, Greenville, SC to Martyr BG Ali Flaih AB, Iraq) 1.2 THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) ONLY. This RFI is issued solely for information and planning purposes � it does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFP in the future. This request for information does not commit the Government to contract for any supply or service whatsoever. Further, the Air Force is not at this time seeking proposals and will not accept unsolicited proposals. Responders are advised that the U.S. Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this RFI; all costs associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the interested party�s expense. Not responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future RFP, if any is issued. If a solicitation is released, it could possibly be synopsized on the SAM.gov website. It is the responsibility of the potential offerors to monitor this site for additional information pertaining to this requirement; however, if you do provide information, you could possibly be sent the solicitation notification directly and this is NOT guaranteed. Background 2.1 The United States Government (USG) has an emerging requirement to execute a point-to-point ferry flight delivery of two (2) F-16 Fighting Falcon (Block 52) aircraft originating from the Lockheed Martin Facility in Greenville, South Carolina (Lockheed Martin F-16 Production and Sustainment Facility, Donaldson Field / KGYH) to Martyr BG Ali Flaih Air Base in the Republic of Iraq. 2.2 Anticipated Execution Period: March 2027. 2.3 Pre-Mission Integration & Approvals: Q1 FY2027 / January�February 2027 (flight records review, GFR approvals, ALSS inspections, APACS clearances, Lockheed Martin site access/badging, and AMC Coronet coordination). 2.4 Operational Division of Responsibility: Contractor Responsibility: Furnish two (2) fully qualified, current, and mission-capable F-16 Block 50/52 Pilot-in-Command (PIC) aviators (plus one designated alternate) to conduct the flight operations. Ensure flight crew compliance with theater entry, medical readiness, survival training standards, and badging/facility access protocols at the Lockheed Martin Greenville facility. Program Office Responsibility: All aircraft maintenance support, pre-/post-flight inspections, en-route servicing, and technical troubleshooting will be coordinated directly by the USG Program Office (e.g., AFLCMC Program Office / designated depot field service teams) in coordination with Lockheed Martin facility personnel prior to release. AMC / ACC Responsibility: All aerial refueling (AAR) support, tanker boom operations, Coronet flight movements, and military oceanic flight plans will be scheduled and coordinated through Air Mobility Command (AMC) and Air Combat Command (ACC). 2.5 Objective The primary objectives of this market research notice are to: Identify commercial sources capable of providing two (2) qualified F-16 Block 52 ferry pilots with documented currency, Pratt & Whitney F100-PW-229 operational familiarity, boom aerial refueling certifications, and international long-range flight experience ready for deployment from the Lockheed Martin Greenville facility to Martyr BG Ali Flaih AB in March 2027. Assess industry capacity to integrate into US Air Force operational flight packages (e.g., cell formation flying and Coronet missions supported by AMC tanker assets) and coordinate closely with Program Office maintenance and plant representatives. Evaluate compliance mechanisms under Defense Contract Management Agency (DCMA) Instruction 8210.1 and Government Flight Representative (GFR) flight crew approval processes operating from a contractor/OEM facility. Solicit industry feedback regarding life support equipment provisioning, survival certifications, theater entry lead times, weather delay/standby structures, and mobilization horizons leading into March 2027. 2.6 Scope of Work and Technical Requirements Areas Task Area 1: Pilot Qualifications, Credentials, and Currency The contractor shall supply two (2) primary ferry pilots and one (1) designated backup/alternate pilot meeting the following mandatory thresholds: Flight Hours & Airframe Currency: Minimum 1,500 total military/tactical flight hours, with at least 500 hours as Pilot-in-Command (PIC) in the F-16. Documented PIC qualification and currency in the F-16 Block 50/52 configuration (Pratt & Whitney F100-PW-229 engine familiarity). Documented F-16 flight currency leading up to the March 2027 departure date (including instrument, formation, and emergency procedures). Aerial Refueling (AAR) Qualification: Current or recent qualification in military boom aerial refueling (day and night tanker receiver procedures) compatible with USAF KC-135, KC-10, or KC-46 tankers. Survival Training & Physiological Standards: Valid Water Survival / Underwater Egress Training (Dunker/HUET) certification current within standard service intervals for oceanic crossings. Valid Physiological / High-Altitude Chamber training (or altitude chamber refresher) compliant with USAF standards. Basic Survival, Evasion, Resistance, and Escape (SERE) familiarization or tactical isolated personnel guidance appropriate for operations into the CENTCOM AOR. Licensing & Medical Certifications: Valid FAA Commercial or Airline Transport Pilot (ATP) Certificate with instrument rating, or military equivalent documentation (DD Form 759 / Flight Record). Current FAA Class I Medical Certificate (or military flight physical equivalent) valid through the planned mission window in March 2027, along with CENTCOM medical deployment readiness/waiver screening. Security Clearance, COMSEC & Facility Access: Active U.S. Secret security clearance (or higher) to handle classified flight route data, secure tactical communication suites (e.g., Have Quick, ARC-210), and Mode 4/5 IFF systems. Eligibility for security vetting and unescorted flight line badge access at the Lockheed Martin Greenville facility. Task Area 2: Operational Coordination and Mission Execution Pre-Flight at Lockheed Martin Facility and Operations with AMC/ACC: Report to the Lockheed Martin facility in Greenville, SC for mission planning, final pre-flight walkarounds, cockpit checks, and coordination with Program Office and DCMA plant personnel. Integrate into AMC Coronet movement planning, mission briefings, and cell lead/trail formation procedures scheduled for the March 2027 movement. Coordinate with Program Office maintenance personnel for aircraft acceptance, debriefings, and aircraft turnover at intermediate staging points and final delivery. Conduct pre-flight route briefings, weather checks, oceanic contingency planning, and divert emergency reviews alongside government tanker/escort crews. DCMA 8210.1 & GFR Approval: Compliance with DCMA Instruction 8210.1 (Contractor's Flight and Ground Operations). Submission of flight crew records, training certificates, and medical approvals to the cognizant Government Flight Representative (GFR) for flight crew qualification approval at least 45 days prior to the March 2027 departure. Theater Entry, International Clearances, and Repatriation: Ensure all flight crew members maintain valid U.S. Passports (minimum 6 months validity past mission window), required en-route transit visas, and Iraqi entry documentation. Coordinate country clearance submissions via the Aircraft Clearance Processing System (APACS) and contractor tracking through the Synchronized Predeployment and Opera

title: NAS WHITING FIELD AIRFIELD PAVEMENT REPAIRS
description: Project Labor Agreement (PLA) Request for Information (RFI) for Construction Project for Airfield Pavement Repairs in the State of Florida This is a request for information/market survey. This is not a request for proposal, request for quote, or an invitation for bid. There will be no solicitation, specification, or drawings available at this time. Naval Facilities Engineering System Command (NAVFAC) Southeast is soliciting comments from the public addressing the potential use of Project Labor Agreements (PLA) for the following construction project. The construction project is for the Airfield Pavement Repairs located at Naval Air Station Whiting Field, Milton, Florida. Construction may include, but is not limited to, repairing the airfield pavement by mill, overlay, and restripe pavement sections within the north airfield at NAS Whiting Field, including Runway 05-23, Runway 14-32, Taxiway A, Taxiway B, Taxiway C, Taxiway D, Taxiway E, Taxiway F, Taxiway G, Taxiway HL, Taxiway NL, Taxiway APPC, and the adjacent Parking Areas. Approximate total concrete pavement repair area is approximately 800,000 square yards. Repairs will include barricades, saw cutting, milling, asphalt overlay, sweeping and preparing pavement surfaces. Minor repairs to concrete pavement include spall repair and joint replacement. The grade adjacent to the runway shoulder pavement edges will be re-graded, compacted and sodded for positive drainage. All airfield pavement markings will be replaced and the airfield lighting removed and replaced as required, reinstalled and adjusted to enable milling and overlay in accordance with UFC 3-260-01 Airfield and Heliport Planning and Design, UFC 3-260-02 Pavement Design for Airfields, and NAVAIR 51-50AAA-2 General Requirements for Shore based Airfield Marking and Lighting. New airfield markings (striping and numbers) will be applied in accordance with current FAA criteria and UFC 3-260-04 Airfield and Heliport Marking. located in the State of Florida. Project will be design-bid-build. NAICS Code: 237310. The magnitude of construction is anticipated to be $25M � $100M. General period of performance is anticipated to be approximately 540 calendar days. A PLA is defined as a pre-hire collective bargaining agreement with one or more labor organizations that establishes the terms and conditions of employment for a specific construction project and is an agreement as described in 29 U.S.C. 158 (f). Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) policy states: Executive Order (E.O.) 14063, Use of Project Labor Agreements for Federal Construction Projects, requires agencies to use PLAs in large-scale construction projects (defined as a construction projects with a total estimated cost at or above $35M) to promote economy and efficiency in the administration and completion of Federal construction projects. When awarding a contract in connection with a large-scale construction project, agencies shall require use of a PLA for contractors and subcontractors engaged in construction on the project, unless an exception(s) at FAR 22.504(d) applies. Reference is made to: FAR Subpart 22.5 Use of Project Labor Agreements for Federal Construction Projects; provision, FAR 52.222-33 Notice of Requirement for Project Labor Agreement; and to clause, FAR 52.222-34 Project Labor Agreement. In consideration of the above factors, and any others which may be deemed appropriate, the public is invited to provide responses on the use of a PLA for this construction project utilizing the attached questionnaire. This is not an announcement of the availability of a solicitation nor is it a means of generating a plan holder�s list. This survey is for planning purposes only and shall not be construed as a Request for Proposal or as an obligation on the part of the Government. The Government does not intend to award a contract on the basis of this market survey or otherwise pay for the requested information. The Government will not provide a debriefing on the results of this survey. All information will be held in a confidential manner and will only be used for the purposes intended. Responses shall be submitted on the attached questionnaire via email to Cynthia McMonigle at cynthia.a.mcmonigle.civ@us.navy.mil, and cc: Aimee Johnson at aimee.n.johnson2.civ@us.navy.mil. no later than 3:00 PM Eastern Time on 11/24/2026.

description: GSA Fleet Lease Vehicle Auction & Marshalling Services 1.0 Description The General Services Administration (GSA) Office of Fleet Management (GSA Fleet) has a requirement to acquire contractor support for vehicle auction and marshalling services or marshalling only services for Government vehicles. Services are required on or about January 1, 2027 � April 30, 2030 in Idaho Falls, ID. Interested parties must be located within 50 miles of the Idaho Falls, ID area. The vendor must be the owner or legal lessee of the facility. Auction and marshalling site tasks include, but are not limited to: Advise the government on optimal disposition strategy for individual exchange/sale-eligible vehicles worldwide to maximize public participation and net proceeds, to include strategies for specialty (law enforcement, buses, ambulances, medium & heavy trucks, etc.) as well as Zero Emission Vehicles to include battery electric vehicles, plug-in hybrid vehicles and/or fuel cell vehicles. Perform full vehicle inspections and ensure complete condition reporting, imagery capture (including high-definition photo and video, 360� views, etc.), and accurate description writing. Provide recommendations on vehicle repairs and pricing, given vehicle condition, market environment, among any other factors, to ensure the greatest return on investment. Create and execute marketing plans/campaigns to catalog vehicles and announce vehicle sales to the public as required by law, and to advertise to/connect with the broadest possible market audience. Perform electronic inventory management for vehicles and vehicle-related assets (e.g., license plates, removed equipment, telematics devices). Support the creation and management of all required vehicle disposition documentation/records. Conduct activities related to bidder/buyer management, including registration, validation/eligibility checks, etc. Provide end-to-end customer service and support to bidders/buyers throughout the sales process to ensure a seamless, transparent, and customer-centric buying experience. Facilitate and perform payment collection process. Encourage maximum participation by offering a range of non-government affiliated services (retail financing, aftermarket warranties, vehicle enhancement etc.). Store, service and remarket of electric vehicles to include any necessary charging infrastructure. Transport vehicles to and from vendor locations. Prepare vehicles for public inspection and final sales/disposition, including services such as reconditioning, maintenance and repair, as well as equipment removal/disposal, and license plate & government credit card disposal and tracking. Offer industry-aligned services for customers to perform vehicle test drives. Provide state-of-the-art technology that will improve customer experience including enhanced condition reporting, 360� views, video, high-definition photography, etc. Conduct a full and open competitive sales process, including public inspection periods for all vehicles, and any related sale services for exchange/sale property. Ensure and facilitate the security, storage, and release of vehicles from time of receipt until final removal. Manage the logistics of vehicle transportation to bring vehicles to sale. Prepare vehicles for sale, to include vehicle equipment removal/disposal, reconditioning, and repairs. Work with local government entities to facilitate any inspections, documentation, and any other actions required to complete transactions in local markets. Perform electronic inventory management, vehicle inspection, complete condition reporting for vehicles. Offer recommendations on vehicle repairs and pricing, given vehicle condition, local market environment, among any other factors, to ensure the greatest return on investment. Provide customer service to buyers in global markets. Create and execute marketing campaigns for local markets. Offer an internet sales platform with the potential to reach a global audience. Collect proceeds from vehicle sales and if necessary, convert to U.S. dollars. Marshalling only site tasks include, but are not limited to: Transport or resource/transportation of vehicles to and from vendor location (e.g., customer location, OEM dealership, offsite repair facility). Inspect vehicles upon delivery for various factors including but not limited to any damage to the vehicle, all components of the vehicle are accounted for (e.g., keys, floor mats, etc.), and missing equipment. Perform telematics device installation and/or activation on all new vehicles prior to releasing the vehicle to the customer. Validate new vehicles and options to vehicle order information provided by GSA. Perform pre-delivery inspections (PDI) in accordance with the manufacturer�s standards. Prepare new vehicles for customer receipt. Provide driver education for customers including vehicle operation, unique features, infotainment settings, etc. Offer specialized expertise and support on Electric Vehicle management, operation and charging infrastructure. Charge battery-powered vehicles. Maintain all vehicle fuel and charge levels as prescribed in the Statement of Work by GSA. Perform custodial and sales preparation services to facilitate auction house sales of GSA exchange lease vehicles. Process and manage all required vehicle shipment and delivery documentation. Manage scheduled vehicle appointments and ensure accurate vehicle exchanges. Perform all necessary tasks associated with confirming vehicle assignment and termination to and from the customer as prescribed by GSA. Provide end-to-end customer service and support to GSA Fleet and customer agencies throughout the marshalling process to ensure a seamless and transparent delivery and exchange process. Fulfill proper disposal of old/expired plates both front and back as prescribed by GSA. Perform electronic inventory management for vehicles. Ensure and facilitate the security, storage and inventory control of vehicles, license plates, credit cards and other assets from time of receipt until final removal. Scale charging capabilities to meet the needs of increasing electric vehicle adoption. 2.0 Background GSA Fleet provides a full-service fleet management program providing transportation solutions to partner agencies worldwide across the U.S. Federal government. It maintains a diverse fleet of over 227,000 vehicles, including light, medium, and heavy-duty vehicles, to include sedans, SUVs, vans, trucks, buses, ambulances, and law enforcement vehicles. Vehicles range from gasoline and diesel fueled vehicles to alternative fuel vehicles (AFVs), such as electric vehicles (EVs) to low-speed electric vehicles (LSEV�s) and non-powered vehicles and trailers. Nationally, GSA Fleet orders and receives on average 30,000+ vehicles from suppliers annually. As GSA Fleet is responsible for the disposition of its vehicles, it then remarkets and sells the used vehicles across the United States and its territories, Japan, and Europe. Its vehicles are sold under the exchange/sale authority of 41 CFR 102-39. This authority aims to expedite the disposal process and maximize proceeds in the most cost-effective manner to the U.S. taxpayer.
