REQUIREMENTS The contractor shall maintain a quality control system which meets the requirements of Mil-I-45208A, Mil-Q 9858,ISO-9000 / 9001 / 9002 or equivalent. RESPONSIBILITY FOR INSPECTION: Unless otherwise specified, the contractor is responsible for the performance of all inspection requirements as specified herein. Except as otherwise specified, the contractor may use his own or any other facility suitable for the performance of the inspection requirements specified herein. PROCEDURES:The contractor shall prepare and maintain Quality Control Documentation, test and repair procedures, and inspection procedures which shall be made available to the Government for review and approval. The procedures shall include sequential diagrams of the test, repair, and inspection process, as well as the performance spcifications to perform the procedures. QUALITY ASSURANCE PROGRAM PLAN: The contractor shall develop, implement and maintain a Repair Quality Plan in compliance with the requirements of Mil-I-45208A, Mil-Q-9858, ISO,9000 / 9001 / 9002, or equvalent.The plan shall define the specific methods by which compliance with contractual requirements will be assured. All quality assurance data shall be provided to the Government for review and approval upon request. PURCHASED MATERIAL CONTROL: The contractor shall establish and maintain a system of control over purchased material which shall assure that the necessary requirements of this contract are included. in all sub contract agreements. A parts control system shall establish a record of performance for each purchased and internally manufactured part and shall be used to evaluate continued use of the source. The contractors control system shall be in compliance wil either Mil-I 45208A/Mil-Q-9858 or equivalent Quality Quality Assurance Standared.(ISO/AS:9000, 9001, 9002). RECEIVING INSPECTION OF PURCHASED MATERIAL: Purchased items shall be inspected upon receipt at the contractors facility to assure conformance with all requirements of the Technical Data Package (TDP). Evidence of such inspections shall be maintained for Government review at least twelve (12) months following acceptance of the end item. Inspection reports shall be maintained by the contractor. The inspection report shall, at a minimum, include a record of all dimensional data (coordinate/positional), material, finish, and process with appropriate pass/fail criteria, such ascertifications, and actual dimensional readings. FAILURE ANALYSIS AND CORRECTIVE ACTION:All failure analysis and corrective action reports/plans shall be submitted to the Government. NONCONFORMING MATERIAL:The contractor shall establish an effective system for controlling nonconforming material including procedures for identification, segregation, and disposition. CONTRACTOR INTERNAL REVIEW BOARD (IRB):IRB authority is delegated to the contractor for this contract only. The IRB may be used only for disposition of materials exhibiting minor non-conformances, scrap or rework to return a part to conformance with drawings or specifications as authorized by the approved repair procedures.IRB shall not use "AS-IS" disposition. A complete file of IRB actions shall be maintained for review by the Government for concurrance of classification. MATERIAL REVIEW BOARD (MRB):Formal MRB authority for disposition of "AS-IS"and for minor non-conformances is retained by the Government. The contractor shall submit the appropriate request for Variance via the DCMC to the NAVSUP Contracting Officer. RESPONSIBILITY FOR COMPLIANCE: All items must meet all requirements of this Statement of Work. The inspection requirements set forth in this SOW shall become part of the contractors overall inspection system or quality program. The absence of any inspection requirements in the SOW shall not relieve the contractor of the responsibility of assuring that all Government equipment submitted for acceptance comply with all requirements. Sampling in quality conformance does not authorize submission of known defective items, either indicated or actual, nor does it commit the procuring activity to acceptance of any defective items. REPAIR ASSESSMENT TESTING: The Government may select samples of the Contract Line Items (CLINS) which have completed repair and have been accepted by the Government representative for the purpose of conducting performance testing, environmental testing, and quality conformance examination in a repair assessment test program. A quantity of CLIN's may be randomly selected from each quaterly repair production completion for shipment to the CFA or other Government designated location to conduct this testing. RECORDS OF DATA COLLECTION: The contractor shall maintain a historical record file to contain copies of applicable data and documents for individual CLIN's and assemblies by CLIN serial number. The historical record file shall include,but not be limited to the following types of historical records: Receipt inspection documentation. Repair shop travelers or repair cards. Parts replacement records. Parts inspection data before and after repair as applicable. Acceptance test data. QA personnel shall maintain a complete receipt inspection,test, repair re-test, history card for each item processed. This information shall be made available to the Government upon request. 4. QUALITY ASSURANCE PROVISIONS - NOT APPLICABLE. 5. PACKAGING- MIL-STD 2073 PACKAGING APPLIES AS FOUND ELSEWHERE IN THE SCHEDULE 6. NOTES - NOT APPLICABLE

title: CBRND Seeking Aircraft Interior Decontamination Technology
description: The Department of War (DoW), Portfolio Management Executive for Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear Defense (PME CBRND), Joint Project Manager for CBRN Special Operations Forces (JPM CBRN SOF) is seeking information, design concepts, and mature technology capabilities for a Tactical Aircraft Interior Decontamination Dispersal System. The goal of this initiative is to identify or evaluate a mature, rapidly deployable, and highly reliable hardware applicator system capable of delivering fine-aerosol, dry-fog, or gaseous decontaminants uniformly throughout military aircraft interiors without damaging sensitive electronics. Key Technical Parameters & Scope: Dispersal Mechanics: Must disperse a fine aerosol/dry fog with a Volume Median Diameter (VMD) of less than 10 microns (Threshold) or a gas-phase molecular dispersion less than 0.001 microns (Objective) to maximize surface coverage without wetting, pooling, or dripping. Tactical Mobility & Footprint: Must fit securely within a Polaris MRZR cargo bed with a stowed envelope not exceeding 42" H x 18" D x 18" W (Threshold), with a target envelope under 30" H x 14" D x 16" W (Objective) to allow upright walk-through clearance in CH-47 and CV-22 cabins. System Weight: Empty chassis weight must be ? 150 lbs (Threshold) for a 4-man lift, with a target empty weight of ? 100 lbs (Objective) for a 2-man lift. Fully loaded weight with maximum consumables must not exceed 500 lbs. Power Flexibility: Operable from standard single-phase 110-120 VAC (50/60 Hz), commercial/tactical generators ? 6 kW, or vehicle auxiliary 28 VDC (Threshold), with a target capability to interface directly with utility and flight-line power IAW MIL-STD-704 (Objective). Employment Versatility: Must support two primary delivery modes: Internal cabin placement on medium/heavy aircraft (CH-47, CV-22, C-130) and external ducting/pumping into constrained cockpits (AH/MH-6 Little Bird). Material Compatibility: All wetted paths, seals, pumps, and nozzles must demonstrate broad chemical compatibility with existing and emerging USG-standard decontaminants, including aqueous hydrogen peroxide ($H_2O_2$), modified amine/ammonia solutions, Dahlgren Decon, and JGPD. System Modularity: Complete operational system must consist of 5 or fewer major items (Threshold), with a target of a single, all-in-one consolidated chassis (Objective) containing integrated internal stowage for all cords, hoses, and nozzles. Technology Maturity: The core dispersal technology must be at a demonstrated Technology Readiness Level (TRL) 6 or higher in a relevant operating environment to support near-term military evaluation and procurement.

title: Kansallinen ilmastoriski- ja haavoittuvuustarkastelu
description: Kansallinen ilmastoriski- ja haavoittuvuustarkastelu Maa- ja metsätalousministeriö (”hankintayksikkö”) vastaa ilmastonmuutokseen sopeutumistyön koordinoinnista valtioneuvostotasolla. Ministeriö vastaa kansallisen ilmastonmuutokseen sopeutumissuunnitelman ja sen taustamateriaalien (ml. kansallisen ilmastoriski- ja haavoittuvuustarkastelun) valmistelusta ilmastolain mukaisesti. Maa- ja metsätalousministeriön tarkoituksena on hankkia valtakunnallisen ilmastoriski- ja haavoittuvuustarkastelun suunnittelu, toteutus ja raportointi. Riski- ja haavoittuvuustarkastelun tulosten tulisi olla käytettävissä, kun kansallisen sopeutumissuunnitelman valmistelu aloitetaan seuraavan vaalikauden alussa. Kansallisen ilmastoriski- ja haavoittuvuustarkastelun valmistelun tavoitteena on saada parhaaseen käytettävissä olevaan tietoon perustuva käsitys Suomeen kohdistuvista ilmasto-riskeistä ja haavoittuvuuksista sekä vahvistaa yhteyttä riskien ja haavoittuvuuksien arvioinnin ja sopeutumispolitiikan suunnittelun välillä. Tarkastelun tulee tukea nykyistä vahvemmin sopeutumistoimien kohdentamista niihin riskeihin, vaikutuksiin ja haavoittuvuuksiin, joiden arvioidaan olevan merkittävimpiä suomalaiselle yhteiskunnalle. Samalla tarkastelun tulisi tunnistaa uusia tai tarkentaa tietoa aiemmin tunnistetuista riskeistä sekä kuvata mahdollisia tietopuutteita. Ilmastolaki edellyttää alueellista tarkastelua tarpeen mukaan. Hankinnan kohde on kuvattu liitteessä 1 Hankinnan kohteen kuvaus.,

description: Kainuun hyvinvointialueen viralliset ilmoitukset ja kuulutukset julkaistaan hyvinvointialuelain mukaisesti hyvinvointialueen verkkosivustolla (hyvinvointialue.kainuu.fi). Tarvittaessa ja harkinnan mukaan ilmoituksia voidaan julkaista myös alueen tiedotusvälineissä (hyvinvointilaki 34 § ja 113 §). Hyvinvointialueen tavoitteena on julkaista tarvittavia asukas- ja asiakastiedotteita tai muita hyvinvointialueen ilmoituksia omien digitaalisten kanavien lisäksi tiedotusvälineissä maksettuina ilmoituksina ensisijaisesti Kainuun ilmaisjakelulehdissä. Tarpeen mukaan ilmoituksia kohdennetaan julkaisualueelle paikallisesti tai alueellisesti. Kainuun hyvinvointialue ei tilaajana sitoudu julkaisevaan tahoon, julkaistavien ilmoitusten määrään, kokoon tai julkaisutiheyteen. Ilmoituksia voidaan julkaista tilaajan tarpeen ja harkinnan mukaisesti myös muissa kuin Hilla Group OyJ:n medioissa. title: Hammastekniset työt; oikomiskojeet ja protetiikka
description: Kainuun hyvinvointialue (Tilaaja) pyytää tarjouksia hammasteknisistä töistä ja palveluista, jotka on tarkemmin määritelty myöhemmin tässä tarjouspyyntöasiakirjassa. Hankittaviin suun terveydenhuollon palveluihin sisältyvät osa-alueina mm. oikomiskojeet ja protetiikka. Sopimuskausi on suunniteltu alkavaksi 1.1.2027 ja päättyvän 31.12.2028. Varsinaisen sopimuskauden jälkeen tilaajalla on oikeus jatkaa sopimuskautta kahdella (2) yhden vuoden (1) mittaisella optiokaudella, jolloin optiokausien kanssa sopimuskausi on yhteensä 2+1+1 vuotta. Optiokaudella sovelletaan sopimusta entisin ehdoin, sen mukaisesti kuin ehdot ovat voimassa perussopimuskauden päättyessä. Hankintasopimuksen piiriin valitaan kaikki kelpoisuus- ja vähimmäisvaatimukset täyttävät tarjoajat. Valitut toimittajat asettuvat osa-alueittain tarjoushinnan perusteella etusijajärjestykseen. Edullisimman hinnan tarjonnut palveluntuottaja sijoittuu etusijajärjestyksessä ensimmäiseksi, toiseksi edullisin toiseksi ja niin edelleen. Mikäli kaksi tai useampi tarjoaja saa saman pistemäärän, etusijajärjestys arvotaan. Kyseessä ei ole puitejärjestely, vaan usean toimittajan hankintasopimus-kokonaisuus. Etusijajärjestyksestä voidaan poiketa kokonaisuus- tai osa-aluetasolla erityisestä potilaskohtaisesta, hammaslääketieteellisesti ja objektiivisesti arvioitavasta perusteesta johtuen. Tällöin tilaaja (lähettävä hammaslääkäri) määrittää ja perustelee potilaan yksilöllisen tarpeen mukaisen, työ- ja potilaskohtaisesti sopivamman palveluntuottajan kyseisen työn tekijäksi. Tilauksissa otetaan myös huomioon potilaan itsemääräämisoikeus terveydenhuollon palveluissa eli potilaan oma tahto ja toive tämän palveluun liittyvissä tekijöissä. Terveydenhuollon palveluissa potilasta pitää hoitaa yhteisymmärryksessä potilaan kanssa, mikä voi johtaa etusijajärjestyksestä poikkeamiseen. Hankinnan sopimuksen alaisten tuotteiden ja niihin liittyvän palvelun tilaajana toimii Kainuun hyvinvointialue, joka järjestää julkiset sosiaali- ja terveydenhuollo ja pelastustoimen palvelut Kainuussa. Hyvinvointialue toimii 8 kunnan alueella Hyrynsalmella, Kajaanissa, Kuhmossa, Paltamossa, Puolangalla, Ristijärvellä, Sotkamossa ja Suomussalmella. Perusterveydenhuolto Kainuun hyvinvointialueen perusterveydenhuollolla tarkoitetaan hyvinvointialueen järjestämää väestön terveydentilan seurantaa, terveyden edistämistä ja erilaisia terveyspalveluita. Hyvinvointialueen on järjestettävä asukkailleen suun terveydenhuollon palvelut. Palveluihin kuuluvat väestön suunterveyden seuranta, terveysneuvonta- ja tarkastukset, suun sairauksien oikea-aikainen tutkimus, ehkäisy ja hoito, sekä asiakkaan hoidon tarpeen varhainen havaitseminen sekä ohjaaminen sosiaali- ja terveydenhuollon muihin palveluihin. Suun terveydenhuollossa hoidetaan perusterveydenhuollon osalta mm. potilaiden purennan kuntoutuksia, hampaiston purentavirheitä ja proteettisia tarpeita. Erikoissairaanhoito Kainuun keskussairaalan suu- ja leukasairauksien poliklinikalla hoidetaan vaikeita purentavirheitä sekä kasvojen ja leukojen alueen tapaturmapotilaita sekä uniapneapotilaita. Suu- ja leukasairauksien poliklinikalla hoidetaan myös kasvojen ja suun alueen syöpäpotilaita, joilla on laajoja kudospuutoksia syöpähoitojen jäljiltä sekä asiakkaita, joilta puuttuu synnynnäisesti useita hampaita. Hoito vaatii usein oikomishoitoa, kirurgista hoitoa ja proteettista purennan kuntoutusta. Hoidossa voidaan tarvita kiinteää ja irtoprotetiikkaa ja implanttiprotetiikkaa. Suu- ja leukasairauksien poliklinikalla hoidetaan myös hampaiden kiinnityskudos- ja kovakudossairauksia, purentafysiologisia sairauksia ja limakalvosairauksia. Erikoissairaanhoidon puolella tehtävät purennan kuntoutukset, oikomishoito ja tarvittavat proteettiset ratkaisut ovat vaativampia kuin perusterveydenhuollon puolella. Palveluntuottajan hammasteknikko tulee olla mahdollista pyytää käymään Kainuun keskussairaalan suu- ja leukasairauksien poliklinikalla erikseen sovittuna ajankohtana, jotta on mahdollista suunnitella, myös potilaan läsnä ollessa, yhdessä proteettisen työn suunnittelu ja toteutus. title: Polar Rover for Observation, Mapping, and In-Situ Exploration (PROMISE) Mission
description: Refurbishment, qualification, and delivery of a scientific radiation measurement instrument to support lunar surface exploration activities associated with the Polar Rover for Observation, Mapping, and In-Situ Exploration (PROMISE) mission. Efforts include engineering analysis, environmental testing, systems integration support, mission operations support, and scientific data analysis associated with the collection and interpretation of radiation measurements on the lunar surface. Some of the efforts require the development and refinement of specialized software tools, data processing techniques, and operational methodologies to support instrument integration, data collection, and analysis throughout the mission lifecycle. The instrument Principal Investigator (PI) and team must have extensive experience in the design, development, testing, operation, and scientific analysis of spaceflight radiation instruments supporting planetary exploration missions. Team members shall work on the original design, fabrication, qualification, and operation of the instrument and have supported the collection and analysis of scientific data for an extended operational period. The current version of the instrument is based on their original design and flight hardware and software development. Additionally, the team has developed specialized software programs, operational processes, and analytical algorithms necessary to support instrument performance assessment, data processing, and scientific interpretation. The team will provide technical support for instrument refurbishment, flight qualification, integration, mission operations, and scientific investigations in support of PROMISE mission objectives.

title: Solutions for Intelligence Analysis 4 (SIA 4)
description: SUBJECT: Request for Information (RFI) for non-personal services to support the Solutions for Intelligence Analysis 4 (SIA 4) Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) 1. INTRODUCTION It is the Virginia Contracting Activity�s (VaCA�s) policy to foster productive exchanges of information between the Government and vendors before issuing requests for proposals (RFPs). This is a Request for Information (RFI) only. This is not a solicitation or RFP. The Government will not award any contracts based solely on this RFI, nor will the Government pay for any costs incurred in responding to this announcement. No RFP currently exists; therefore, please do not request a copy of the RFP. Due to the intelligence nature of the anticipated requirements, the Solutions for Intelligence Analysis 4 (SIA 4) procurement will be classified. Following the conclusion of this RFI, anticipate all future SIA 4 procurement actions will be released through the National Reconnaissance Office (NRO) Acquisition Resource Center (ARC). The Government anticipates that all vendor proposals will be classified. Vendors desiring to participate in this procurement should prepare now to ensure they have the required access and ability to respond. As part of its market research, VaCA is issuing this RFI to determine if an adequate number of qualified interested vendors exists with the requisite experience and skill sets required to provide intelligence analysis and analytics supporting professional services. Given the complexity and technical nature of Defense Intelligence Enterprise (DIE) requirements, high levels of analytical intelligence expertise, tradecraft, and mission area knowledge are essential to providing the most accurate and highest quality intelligence support possible. In addition to identifying potential sources, vendor input is sought to clarify commercial industry terminology and approach. Responses to this RFI will be assessed for the purpose of market research, information and planning purposes only. As such, industry responses will not be treated as proposals. The Government further reserves the right to terminate this request and change its requirements if needed. Responding to this RFI does not guarantee participation in future Government activities. Responses to this RFI are not considered offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form binding contracts. Response to this RFI is not mandatory for participation in the SIA 4 solicitation. Vendors should be advised that all submissions become Government property. Responses to this RFI will not be returned. 2. PURPOSE This document serves as the RFI of the VaCA vendor community pursuant to RFO 15.101 �Early exchanges with industry.� VaCA is conducting preliminary planning and market research to enable design and release of an SIA 4 RFP. VaCA is issuing this RFI to open the announcement and early participation to the full market so that all high-potential sources of support can be identified across industry. The goal is to identify the portion of the market that can provide the best competition for the SIA 4 follow-on contract, including both established providers and new entrants with relevant capabilities. As this will be a classified procurement, it is the responsibility of the interested parties to monitor the NRO ARC for updates and to prepare now to ensure they have the access and ability to respond through secure channels subsequent to this RFI. Responses to this RFI will be assessed to identify sources that are considered best qualified to meet future requirements. Best qualified sources are those sources which demonstrate the greatest depth and breadth of skills, experiences, and knowledge relevant to the mission, goals, and objectives of the VaCA. 3. BACKGROUND As a follow-on to the current SIA 4 contract vehicle, SIA 4 is planned to be a non-personal services contract for intelligence analytics support to the VaCA and the DIE. Services are anticipated both in CONUS and OCONUS. In some cases, OCONUS services will subject personnel to harsh and hostile conditions in environments designated by the U.S. Government as Imminent Danger and / or Hostile Fire Zones. 4. ANTICIPATED SCOPE OF WORK Once solicitated, the Government intends to award prime contracts to multiple companies, including small businesses. It is the policy of the Government to provide maximum practicable opportunities in its procurements to small and disadvantaged businesses. To support future small business requirements, all prime contract awardees MUST include as part of their team at time of proposal submission small businesses representing the four primary set-aside categories � small disadvantaged business (SDB) (including 8(a)-certified SDB), woman owned small business (WOSB), service-disabled veteran owned small business (SDVOSB), and historically under-utilized business zone (HUBZONE). The planned period of performance (PoP) for the anticipated multiple award IDIQ contracts will be a five (5) year base ordering period with one optional five (5) year ordering period. title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source - Aalyria Technologies, Inc.
description: NASA/Space Communications and Navigation (SCaN) - Network Integration division at NASA Marshal Space Flight Center (MSFC) has a requirement for a common network orchestration layer connecting SCaN's ground antennas, in-space satellites, control centers, and mission users across a heterogeneous set of both government-owned and commercial networks. SCaN's network portfolio has historically consisted of a limited number of government-owned and vertically integrated networks such as the Deep Space Network (DSN) and Near Space Network (NSN). This portfolio is rapidly evolving into a more complex ecosystem comprising: Near-Earth � The Communications Services Project (CSP) provides commercial space-relay services, succeeding the TDRS relay function. Cislunar � LEGS (ground / Direct-with-Earth) and LCRNS (orbital relay and navigation) extend coverage to the Moon, including the far side and south pole. Mars � The Mars Telecommunications Network (MTN) provides a dedicated relay at Mars. Each of these networks arrives with its own operations complex, ground or relay system, scheduling process, and service interface. Left unintegrated, this diversity becomes the responsibility of individual NASA missions, which must separately discover, request, schedule, and monitor services from each network they touch. A unified Enterprise Service Management Network Orchestration Platform (ENOP) capability is needed to realize the "One Network" vision for SCaN network operations. The objective of this effort is to establish a single, unified ENOP capability such that the union of multiple SCaN systems behave as a unified network supporting an extensible set of missions. NASA/Information Technology Procurement Office (ITPO) intends to issue a sole source contract to acquire the services from: Aalyria Technologies, Inc. 7633 Southfront RD STE 200 Livermore, California 94551-8223, United States Aalyria Technologies, Inc. is the only responsible source capable of satisfying the agency requirements under the authority of FAR 6.103-1. The Government intends to acquire a commercial product or service using FAR Part 12. Interested organizations may submit their capabilities and qualifications to perform the effort electronically via email to Nicolas Zogaib at nicolas.a.zogaib@nasa.gov not later than 5:00PM ET on 11/24/2026. Such capabilities/qualifications will be evaluated solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct this acquisition on a competitive basis. A decision by the Government not to compete this acquisition on a full and open competition basis, based upon responses to this notice, is solely within the discretion of the Government. title: Market Intelligence Notice: Fort Hood Bldg 410 General Stilwell Army Reserve Center (ARC)
description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) / MARKET INTELLIGENCE NOTICE This is a Request for Information (RFI) for market intelligence and for informational purposes only. This announcement does not constitute a Solicitation or a Request for Proposal (RFP), and no solicitation is currently available. Participation in this RFI is strictly voluntary. The Government will not be obligated to award any agreement or contract because of this RFI, nor will it reimburse respondents for any costs associated with the preparation or submission of information. Submitting a response will not affect a firm�s ability to submit a proposal should formal solicitation be issued in the future. NAICS Code: 236220 � Commercial and Institutional Building Construction (Note: While Other Transaction Authority is not subject to FAR-based small business regulations, this NAICS code is provided for market research to help the Government understand the size and demographics of the interested industrial base.) Small Business Size Standard: $45 Million PROJECT OVERVIEW The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Louisville District, has a requirement for the design and construction of a project to repair, restore, and modernize Building 410 � the General Stilwell Army Reserve Center (ARC) � a failing two-story, 144,360 SF Command and Control / training facility, along with Non-Organizational (POV) parking and supporting utilities, located at Fort Hood, Texas. The scope of work consists of furnishing all necessary design services, equipment, materials, labor, construction management, supervision, quality control, and supplies to deliver a fully functional, code-compliant, and modernized facility that extends the economic life of the building by 25 years and enables mission readiness for the assigned Army Reserve units. Building 410 was constructed in November 1985 and provides mission-essential functional areas in support of six Legal Detachments, a Training Brigade, Transportation Company, Civil Affairs Brigade, Human Resources Company Headquarters, a Public Affairs Detachment, and the Reserve Personnel Action Center. The mechanical, plumbing, and electrical systems are beyond their serviceable life. A technical assessment has confirmed widespread facility deterioration. Key facility deficiencies include: � Roof membrane system has exceeded useful life and is past warranty; exterior doors, windows, and storefronts require replacement; interior finishes (walls, flooring, acoustical ceilings) are failing. � HVAC systems (rooftop units, air handlers, boilers, pumps, piping, radiation units, controls, and exhaust fans) are in failing condition or original to the building. � Electrical infrastructure is original, fully loaded 1600A main panel with no capacity for additional loads; insufficient outlets creating safety hazards; distribution panels and wiring require modernization. � Plumbing fixtures and sanitary piping require code upgrades; hot water heater is undersized. � Telecommunications infrastructure (Category 5/6 cabling) is unreliable and does not comply with current Army Reserve Network Enterprise Center (ARNEC), TIA-607, or UFC 3-580-01 standards; no Primary or Secondary Bonding Busbars. � No fire sprinkler system; bathrooms do not meet ADA standards; facility lacks an elevator; telecommunication spaces are undersized. � Hazardous materials (asbestos and lead-based paint) identified throughout the facility requiring abatement. SCOPE: The project repairs and restores Building 410 by addressing widespread facility deterioration and returning the structure to a fully functional, code-compliant training facility. Work includes comprehensive repairs to failing electrical, plumbing, and heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) systems, along with full rehabilitation of the building envelope, including roof replacement. The facility will be brought up to Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) standards. The project will demolish and abate all failing components and hazardous materials. Asbestos, mold, lead-based paint, biohazard, or other hazardous materials will be handled, stored, and disposed of in accordance with current laws and regulations. Supporting work includes Non-Organizational Vehicle Parking and Supporting Utilities improvements. Other methods of meeting this requirement were analyzed, including building demolition and new construction; however, these were deemed unviable due to the cost of repair versus the cost of demolition and new construction. The repair of this facility is more cost effective than replacement. Estimated Acquisition Magnitude: $90,000,000 PRIMARY ACQUISITION STRATEGY UNDER EVALUATION: Progressive Design Build (PDB) via Other Transaction Authority (OTA). The Louisville District is evaluating a Progressive Design Build (PDB) strategy utilizing an Other Transaction (OT) Agreement under the authority of 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. This authority is intended for military construction projects that involve testing and experimentation associated with new and emergent construction technologies to achieve potential benefits such as enhanced mission resilience, improved installation support, or cost and schedule reduction. The PDB Course of Action (10 U.S.C. � 2808a): This path allows USACE to execute a construction project where the Construction Firm is brought in during the design. The Louisville District anticipates onboarding the collaborative partner at an appropriate design maturity to maximize value. Phase 1 (Design & Pre-Construction): The Government and the OT Awardee will work collaboratively to advance the design, perform constructability reviews, conduct open-book cost estimating, and mitigate project risks. Phase 2 (Construction): Upon reaching an agreed-upon level of design (e.g., 60% to 90%), the Awardee will propose a Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP). If the GMP is accepted, the Government will exercise Phase 2 for construction execution. If a GMP cannot be agreed upon, the Government retains an "off-ramp" to complete the design and construct the facility via alternative methods. Therefore, the Government is utilizing this RFI to assess industry capability, interest, and the advantages of utilizing PDB utilizing an OT Agreement under the authority of 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. Collaborative Delivery Experience: Describe your experience executing Construction Management at Risk (CM@Risk), Progressive Design Build (PDB), Integrated Design and Construction (IDAC), Early Contractor Involvement (ECI) or other highly collaborative delivery methods.
